content:
CIA declassified file about Yamantau Mountain Underground Construction Project, USSR.

This report analyzes Soviet-era underground construction activity at Mount Yamantau (Ямантау) in the southern Ural Mountains, near what is now the closed town of Mezhgorye (formerly Beloretsk-15/16) in Bashkortostan, Russia.

It includes satellite imagery analysis and assessments of large-scale tunneling and excavation work at the Yamantau site.

U.S. intelligence viewed the project as highly secretive and likely military/strategic in nature.

Construction involved deep tunneling into quartz rock (estimates in related sources place parts at depths of ~3,000 feet), extensive support infrastructure (roads, rail access), and thousands of workers.

Russian/Soviet explanations at the time varied and were often contradictory (e.g., mining operations, ore processing, underground storage for food/archives), but U.S. analysts largely dismissed these as cover stories given the scale, secrecy, and location.

It remains a restricted ZATO (closed administrative-territorial formation) today.
